title: C++ Namespaces, Enums, fstream and std::filesystem: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before notes on C++ namespaces and using declarations, anonymous namespaces, enum vs enum class, file I/O with fstream, and std::filesystem paths and directory iteration.

chapters.title: Namespaces and Name Lookup
points: A namespace groups names to avoid collisions: namespace app { int x; } is accessed as app::x; the same namespace can be reopened across files and extended
A using declaration (using std::cout;) imports one name into the current scope; a using directive (using namespace std;) imports every name and can cause ambiguity
Never put using namespace in a header: it leaks into every file that includes it; limit it to function scope or .cpp files
Namespace alias: namespace fs = std::filesystem; shortens long names, and nested namespaces can be written as namespace a::b::c { } (C++17)
Argument-dependent lookup (ADL): an unqualified call like swap(a, b) also searches the namespaces of the argument types, which is why operator<< for your own type works

chapters.title: Anonymous Namespaces and Internal Linkage
points: namespace { int counter = 0; } gives its members internal linkage: they are visible only inside that translation unit
It is the modern replacement for file-scope static on variables and functions; static is still needed for class members and function-local statics
Two .cpp files can each define the same name in an anonymous namespace with no ODR clash, because each is a separate unique namespace
Names in an anonymous namespace are used unqualified in the same file; do not put one in a header, since each includer gets its own private copy
Use it for file-local helpers and constants; use a named namespace plus a header declaration for anything shared across files

chapters.title: enum vs enum class
points: Unscoped enum { Red, Green } leaks its enumerators into the enclosing scope, so two enums with Red collide, and it converts implicitly to int
Scoped enum class Color { Red, Green }; needs Color::Red, has no implicit conversion to int, and cannot be compared with other enum types
Convert explicitly: static_cast<int>(Color::Red) to get the value, static_cast<Color>(1) to go back; there is no range check on the cast
Choose the underlying type: enum class Status : uint8_t { Ok, Fail }; this allows forward declaration (enum class Status;) and controls size
Prefer enum class by default; use a plain enum only when you need implicit int conversion, such as bit flags with bitwise operators (enum class needs overloaded operators for |)

chapters.title: Reading and Writing Files with fstream
points: Include <fstream>: std::ifstream reads, std::ofstream writes, std::fstream does both; the file closes automatically when the object goes out of scope (RAII)
Always check that the open succeeded: std::ifstream in("a.txt"); if (!in) { /* handle error */ }; a failed open does not throw by default
Read by line with while (std::getline(in, line)) and by token with while (in >> x); put the read in the loop condition, never loop on eof()
Write with std::ofstream out("a.txt"); out << text << '\n'; the default mode truncates the file, and std::ios::app appends, e.g. std::ofstream out(p, std::ios::app)
Mode flags combine with |: std::ios::binary for raw bytes (read/write take char* and a size), std::ios::in, std::ios::out, std::ios::trunc; prefer '\n' over std::endl, which flushes every time

chapters.title: std::filesystem Paths and Directory Iteration
points: Include <filesystem> (C++17) and alias it: namespace fs = std::filesystem; link with -lstdc++fs on old GCC; fs::path is built from a string and uses / to append: fs::path p = dir / "data" / "a.txt"
Path parts: p.filename(), p.stem() (name without extension), p.extension() (includes the dot), p.parent_path(), and p.replace_extension(".csv"); these only manipulate text and never touch the disk
Query the disk with fs::exists(p), is_regular_file(p), is_directory(p), file_size(p); create with create_directories(p), and remove with remove(p) or remove_all(p), which deletes recursively

Iterate one level with for (const auto& e : fs::directory_iterator(dir)); recurse with fs::recursive_directory_iterator(dir); each entry has e.path() and e.is_directory(), and iteration order is unspecified

Most functions throw fs::filesystem_error on failure; pass a std::error_code as the last argument for the non-throwing overload, e.g. fs::exists(p, ec); also, p / "/abs" with an absolute right side replaces the whole path

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Namespaces, Enums, Files
points: Namespaces: ns::name, using ns::name; (one name), namespace x = ns::long::path;, no using namespace in headers
File-local helpers go in namespace { ... } instead of static
enum class E : uint8_t { A, B }; use E::A and static_cast<int>(e) to convert
fstream: ifstream/ofstream, check if (!f), loop with while (getline(f, s)), modes ios::app, ios::binary
filesystem: fs::path / "x", stem(), extension(), exists(), create_directories(), directory_iterator, recursive_directory_iterator, error_code overload to avoid throws
